lab.hero.lede.1.text0: Hanji takes different shapes to suit the ways we share knowledge, exchange ideas, and work with agents. A place to explore what working together can become.
lab.about.p.1.text0: Agents are changing how work gets done, faster than our habits can adapt. We are learning to work alongside new forms of intelligence—and the ways we interact with them are still taking shape.
lab.about.p.2.text0: Hanji’s mission is to bring clarity to those interactions. We build and test small, thoughtful surfaces where people can understand what agents contribute, ask questions, and shape what happens next.
lab.chapter.p.2.text0: Use readable files and open formats so knowledge remains accessible, reusable, and independent of any one interface.
lab.chapter.p.3.text0: Keep proposals, authorship, and discussion connected to the work, so people can review changes with the context they need.
lab.chapter.p.4.text0: Bring shared knowledge into project work. Give agents a defined role while keeping priorities and direction in people’s hands.
lab.projects.p.1.text0: What does collaboration with agents need to feel clear and useful? We began with knowledge sharing, then turned to the work that grows around it.
lab.projects.project-subhead.1.text0: Your agents already live in Git.
lab.projects.p.2.text0: Agents are prolific at creating documents and notes. Knowledge began as a surface for people to read, edit, and build on that work together with agents. Markdown lives in your Git repository; proposed changes stay open to human review.

lab.projects.project-subhead.2.text1: A place to ask what comes next.
lab.projects.p.3.text0: That led to a second question: how should we manage work alongside agents? Tracker explores projects, tasks, and dependencies, with conversations attached to the work so people can see what is happening and guide the next step.

lab.vision.p.1.text0: Hanji is an experimental doorway into a changing world of work. We explore how people and agents can work alongside one another with greater understanding and a clearer sense of direction.
lab.vision.p.2.text0: The surface will keep changing as we learn. Knowledge and Tracker are our first experiments, shaped by the people who use them.
lab.chapter.overline.2.text0: 한지 / A material to think with
lab.chapter.div.2.text0: Hanji takes its name from traditional Korean paper. For us, it is a way to think about software: a thin surface between people and agents, taking different shapes and shades to suit each interaction.
lab.chapter.div.2.text2: A document, a conversation, a project canvas. Different surfaces for the same question: how can we work well together?

tracker.views.p.1.text0: Use the list to review details, the board to track status, and the canvas to understand dependencies. All three views reflect the same issues.

tracker.views.p.2.text0: Pan and zoom through grouped project territories or dependency lanes. Trace a direct link or a whole chain, pin what matters, and fit that chain into view. Parent–child relationships and blockers remain distinct.
tracker.views.p.3.text0: Open an issue alongside the work. Set its owner, status, milestone, or due date; add a comment or adjust a dependency. Saved views, filters, sortable lists, and keyboard navigation help you return to the work that matters.
tracker.chapter.p.1.text0: Discuss a specific issue or start a conversation about the workspace. Address a configured Claude or Codex agent directly, with the relevant work in context.
tracker.chapter.p.2.text0: Developer builds include ongoing Claude and Codex sessions, with permission prompts and controls to stop or continue work. These workflows are still being validated with live agents.

tracker.direction.p.1.text0: Assign project leads, define milestones, and connect issues to key results. Review progress alongside the objectives it supports.
tracker.direction.img.1.alt: Tracker objectives for a fictional project, with a completion result and reader-feedback metric
tracker.direction.span.1.text0: Tracker objectives for a fictional project, with a completion result and reader-feedback metric
tracker.direction.small.1.text0: Open the image to view full size.
tracker.direction.span.2.text0: Progress, measures, and check-ins in the same workspace.
tracker.direction.p.2.text0: Milestones live in project documents. Linked issues supply their progress, while dates make overdue work visible. Group the canvas around a project, person, milestone, or key result.
tracker.direction.p.3.text0: Track metrics, completion, binary results, and rollups. Record check-ins with confidence and a note, so the reason behind a number stays visible too.
tracker.tracker-foundation.p.1.text0: Issues, projects, and posted comments use Markdown. Saved views use YAML. Session state and live events are stored in a local database.
tracker.tracker-foundation.p.2.text0: The web interface, CLI, and MCP tools share the same core. Changes made through the CLI or MCP are attributed in Git. What an agent can change depends on the workflow and its permissions.

  issues/

  projects/
    fieldnotes.md
  objectives/
    o1.md
  threads/
  views/
    launch.yml
  workspace.yml
tracker.chapter.p.3.text0: Practical tools for navigating, organizing, and reviewing work.
tracker.chapter.summary.1.text0: Find your way through the work
tracker.chapter.p.4.text0: Saved YAML views with names and icons. Search, persistent list sorting, and a command menu. Use J/K to move, Enter to open, V to change layout, and ? to see the available shortcuts.
tracker.chapter.summary.2.text0: Shape the workspace as you go
tracker.chapter.p.5.text0: Create and edit projects, capture an idea, and update groups of issues. Assign an owner, priority, labels, due date, milestone, and key result without creating another source of truth.
tracker.chapter.p.6.text0: Canvas chains can reveal prerequisites outside the current view and mark cycles. The CLI’s review command groups work for a weekly review; lint flags things such as stale asks and changed or missing sources.
tracker.chapter.p.7.text0: Optional Knowledge links bring background into the work. Tracker remains useful on its own; connecting a knowledge base is a choice.
tracker.status.p.1.text0: Tracker is in alpha, with access by request. Expect an evolving interface and capabilities. Contact us if you would like to try it and share feedback.
tracker.status.p.2.text0: Tracker shares Hanji’s AGPL-3.0-only license. Public distribution and supported installation are not yet finalized. Hosted team workspaces, individual permissions, importers, and GitHub status synchronization are not currently supported. Build automation still requires live validation before use.

knowledge.availability: Knowledge is in closed beta, with access by request. Contact us to tell us how you would like to use it. The handbook is open to everyone.
knowledge.prerequisites: An existing Knowledge checkout, recent Node.js, pnpm, Git, a C build toolchain, and a folder of Markdown. No model account is needed to read or edit.
knowledge.setup: From the checkout, install dependencies and start the web app. Open localhost:4100.
knowledge.outcome: Name your space, choose an owner password, and select your Markdown folder. Edit one page and press Update: your first change is saved in Git.
knowledge.agent: Connect your coding agent with a scoped token when needed. Your agent account or subscription is managed separately. See the deployment options below for connection details.

tracker.availability: Tracker is in alpha, with access by request. Expect an evolving interface and capabilities. Contact us if you would like to try it and share feedback.
tracker.prerequisites: An existing checkout containing Tracker, recent Node.js, pnpm 9.15, Git, and a C build toolchain for SQLite. You can create and browse tasks without a model account.
tracker.setup: From the checkout, create a fresh workspace, then a project and its first task. Keep this terminal’s workspace variable when starting the web app.
tracker.outcome: Open localhost:4102. Find Fieldnotes and its invitation task in the list or canvas. The project and task are Markdown files in your workspace repository.
tracker.agent: Configure an installed Claude or Codex agent in Setup, authenticate it separately, and start pnpm tracker-host with the same TRACKER_WORKSPACE. Agent sessions remain experimental and are still being validated with live providers.
